findings.title: Unguarded put(span) override breaks build below API level 9
findings.claim: The pure-virtual put(std::span<...>) override is only pure-virtual at Seastar_API_LEVEL >= 9; below that level the build breaks with three errors since the test doesn't use the existing #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 fallback pattern used elsewhere.

findings.title: Regression test never asserts the frame was refused
findings.claim: try/catch around stream_send_empty_frame().get() asserts nothing in either branch, so if send() wrongly accepts the frame the test still passes; only a second-order check that depends on poller timing catches it.

findings.title: Queue-drain half of the fix has no test
findings.claim: Deleting lines 562-568 (the queue_drained handling) leaves the new regression test passing, so this riskier half of the fix, which changes what stop_send_loop() sees, is untested.

findings.title: Comment asserts opposite of what the code does about _outgoing_queue_ready
findings.claim: The comment says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready, but stop_send_loop() does wait on it; the real point (that the wait becomes vacuous after the exchange, with the drain guarantee flowing through _sink_closed_future) is nowhere stated, leaving the invariant unprotected against reordering.

findings.title: send_empty_frame's public contract not updated for new closed_error failure mode
findings.claim: The PR makes send_empty_frame newly fail with closed_error in a window where it previously succeeded, but the doc comment still only describes the old behavior and doesn't warn callers not to treat the failure as fatal.

findings.title: sink::close() can now fail where it previously succeeded, undocumented
findings.claim: Deferring write_buf.close() past a suspension point widens the failure window: if the peer tears down the connection while the drain is parked, output_stream::close() can rethrow a stored exception, a change not mentioned in the commit message or PR body.

findings.title: "Both halves" claim is wrong for one-directional streams
findings.claim: The doc and rpc_types.hh both claim shutdown requires both halves closed, but _sink_closed and _source_closed default to true and are only cleared by the respective impl constructors, so a connection with only a sink never needs a source to close for stream_close() to run.

findings.title: #closing-a-stream anchor is dead in the doxygen build
findings.claim: Because MARKDOWN_ID_STYLE is unset in Doxyfile.in, header IDs become autotoc_md<N> rather than GitHub slugs, so the #closing-a-stream anchor resolves on GitHub but produces an unresolved-reference warning and renders as plain text in the generated API docs.

findings.title: Parked close() has no scope guard, risking SIGABRT or hang
findings.claim: st.release_close.set_value() is a bare statement; any throw between lines 2011 and 2025 leaves it unsatisfied, causing ~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT to fire or the test to hang instead of producing a diagnosable failure, even though defer is already included.

findings.title: Test can't attribute refusal to _stream_closing rather than _error
findings.claim: send() returns closed_error for both _stream_closing and _error, and the test comment claims _error is not yet set but nothing checks it; the ordering that makes the test pass for the right reason is a race the fix could lose without failing the test.

findings.title: Comment names wrong cause for _outgoing_queue_ready exceptional state
findings.claim: The new comment claims _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed, but entry failures are swallowed by send()'s continuation; the real causes are withdraw(it, ex) and _negotiated->set_exception() from a concurrent stop_send_loop(), which the neighboring pre-existing comment states correctly.

findings.title: Lambda parameter f shadows function-scope f being assigned
findings.claim: The lambda parameter f shadows the function-scope f being assigned, making the statement read as f = ...f... in the one place an exception is deliberately discarded; should be renamed to drained.

findings.title: Drain logic worth rewriting as a coroutine matching existing file style
findings.claim: This block would be clearer written as a coroutine, matching the shape already used elsewhere in the file at lines 1066 and 1289, provided the .finally rethrow-after-stop() ordering is preserved.

findings.title: Field comment for closing flag omits scope, lifetime, and naming rationale
findings.claim: The comment for the new flag doesn't say it's stream-connection-only, never cleared, or why _sink_closed wasn't reused (it can't be, since it's true on every connection); the name reads as "the stream is closing" when it means "this connection refuses further sends".

findings.title: New doxygen blocks duplicate legacy comments; \ref source is ambiguous
findings.claim: The new doxygen blocks sit on top of legacy comment lines, leaving two comment blocks per class (cosmetic only, doxygen still associates correctly); also \ref source is ambiguous with connected_socket_impl::source() and should be qualified as \ref rpc::source.

findings.title: "Shut down only once both halves are closed" contradicts line 49
findings.claim: Line 115's claim that the stream shuts down only once both halves are closed contradicts line 49's statement that closing the client aborts any stream still open on it; error paths and peer shutdown also tear it down, so "only" should be dropped.

findings.title: "Dropping an unclosed sink is an error" understates it as an abort
findings.claim: The doc says dropping an unclosed sink is an error, but SEASTAR_ASSERT is documented as active in all build modes, making it an abort in release; also the assert tests the connection's flag, so with two sinks on one connection closing either satisfies it.

findings.title: Hardcoded hooks.size()==2u and dangling reference risk from hooks.back()
findings.claim: BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(hooks.size(), 2u) hardcodes the fixture's connection count rather than testing the code under test, and the reference from hooks.back() could dangle if a push_back happens before it's used 16 lines later; recommends recording size before make_stream_sink and copying the std::function.

findings.title: 10-yield loop comment misdescribes what guarantees progress
findings.claim: The magic 10-yield loop doesn't do what its comment says; yield() only reschedules a task and doesn't force the batch-flush poller to run. What actually guarantees progress is the sink_closed.get()/server_done.get() calls below.

findings.title: negotiate() calls abort() instead of BOOST_FAIL, killing binary without diagnostic
findings.claim: negotiate(feature, is_server) const override calls abort(), which kills the whole test binary with no Boost.Test diagnostic; it copies existing precedent at line 1817, but BOOST_FAIL is the right call.

findings.title: const_cast hack to push_back into hooks instead of declaring mutable
findings.claim: const_cast<...*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) is used instead of declaring hooks mutable.

findings.title: test_sink_state declared inside lambda body risks dangling reference (latent)
findings.claim: test_sink_state st is declared inside the lambda body, but wrappers holding test_sink_state& are owned by the rpc connection, which deferred_stop(cl) tears down after the body returns; latent since nothing touches _st on that path today, but server_factory/client_factory are correctly outside and st should move there.

findings.title: server_done initialized to make_ready_future<>() lets check pass vacuously
findings.claim: future<> server_done = make_ready_future<>() means server_done.get() at line 2028 passes silently even if the server handler never ran.

findings.title: server_factory is wired up but never read, leaving server-side case untested
findings.claim: server_factory is wired up and never read; the symmetric server-side case is untested, and server teardown (including abort_all_streams()) differs enough from the client's that "same base function" isn't a complete argument for coverage.

findings.title: buffer_size() hardcoded to 8192 without comment explaining it's an unused stub
findings.claim: buffer_size() is hardcoded to 8192; verified dead since connected_socket::output() passes an explicit default of 8192 so the sink's value is never consulted and can't be forwarded, but this should be stated in a comment.

findings.title: set_reuseaddr/get_reuseaddr silently dropped rather than forwarded
findings.claim: set_reuseaddr/get_reuseaddr are silently dropped rather than forwarded, matching local precedent at lines 169-170.

findings.title: Block comment describes bug in present tense after it's already fixed
findings.claim: The block comment describes the bug in the present tense after it has been fixed; a reader checking against rpc.cc:293 finds the claim false and can't tell which is stale.

findings.title: Comment about where ~output_stream() asserts is incorrect
findings.claim: The comment claiming "this is where ~output_stream() asserts on the pending batch flush" isn't accurate for this test, since the wrapper forwards put() so the write completes; it actually fails one line earlier at line 2030. The PR description states this correctly but the code comment doesn't.

findings.title: "Pass-through compressor" description is inaccurate and a subtle buffer swap is uncommented
findings.claim: "A pass-through compressor" is inaccurate since it delegates to lz4_fragmented_compressor, and the genuinely subtle line swapping an empty snd_buf for rpc::snd_buf(temporary_buffer<char>()) before delegating is uncommented, both here and at the copy at line 1764.

findings.title: Commits and PR body carry Claude/Anthropic attribution trailers
findings.claim: All three commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers, and the PR body ends with the "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" line, both violating the attribution rule in effect for this repo.

findings.title: Issue references use upstream scylladb/seastar numbers unresolvable in this repo
findings.claim: Fixes #3663 / Refs #3653 are upstream scylladb/seastar issue numbers that resolve to nonexistent issues in dkropachev/ironweave; should use the scylladb/seastar#3663 form.

findings.title: std::exchange on _outgoing_queue_ready could double-move or race
findings.claim: Reviewer checked whether std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, make_ready_future<>()) could double-move or race with stream_close(), and found it safe: _error is set synchronously before its own move with no suspension before the exchange, and withdraw()'s swap migrates the promise correctly; nothing appends to the queue after the exchange.

findings.title: Deferred write_buf.close() could introduce a new deadlock
findings.claim: Reviewer checked for a new deadlock from deferring write_buf.close() and found none: pre-PR the same socket flush already gated stop(), and the negotiation-gated case is unreachable since make_stream_sink() awaits await_connection() before a sink_impl exists.

findings.title: Capturing this across a suspension point in .finally could be a lifetime bug
findings.claim: Reviewer checked lifetime safety of the .finally([this]{ return stop(); }) capture across a suspension point and found it unchanged from pre-existing behavior, since sink_impl/source_impl hold the xshard_connection_ptr for the whole chain.

findings.title: closed_error could be the wrong exception or confuse in-tree callers
findings.claim: Reviewer checked whether closed_error is the right exception and confirmed no in-tree caller is confused: _stream_closing implies _sink_closed so sink_impl::send_buffer and sink_impl::close short-circuit first, the compressor hook is the only reachable caller, and stream_closed would be a lie for a locally initiated close.

findings.title: Discarding the drain exception could be a new silent-failure regression
findings.claim: Reviewer checked whether discarding the drain exception is a regression and found it isn't: stop_send_loop() consumed the same exception identically pre-PR via ignore_ready_future(); the genuine silent failure in this area (send_entry() failures swallowed with no log) predates the PR.

findings.title: Reproducer test could be non-deterministic or rely on stubbed-out behavior
findings.claim: Reviewer checked and found the reproducer deterministic where it matters, since parking data_sink::close() and firing the hook from the test thread pins the window open instead of racing for it; can_batch_flushes() and on_batch_flush_error() are correctly forwarded rather than stubbed.

findings.title: New source contract documentation could be inaccurate
findings.claim: Reviewer checked the new source contract docs ("no close(); read to eof or error", applies on error too) and found them accurate: sink_impl::close() routes through f.finally([con]{ return con->close_sink(); }) even on the error branch.
